The Hitchhikers Guide to Rubric Quality Understanding and Enrichment

paper.arxiv.2604.01375

Prepared 15 Nov 2026 · Evidence snapshot 12 Nov 2026 · Report research-2026-11-12.1 · Evidence research-2026-11-11.candidate.1

Evidence & scope

Substantive bounded primary methods/results/limitations source review is documented at 2604.01375v4. Rubric quality signals/GPT-persona panels and isolated defect-injection limits establish rubric/evaluation methodology. Model personas do not become a human necessity panel. Original author/source-verifier/adversarial receipts bind every exact approved fact; unread pages, unreplicated experiments and source conflicts remain recorded in the pinned dossier. This admission is for one logical paper work only.

Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

The controlled experiment injects one failure mode at a time and assesses absolute weight magnitudes; overlapping real-world failures, non-additive scoring/gates and downstream policy-learning consequences remain outside the experiment.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

The rubric-quality framework combines content validity, domain mapping, cross-lens judging and weight calibration; its scoring panels are five GPT-5.5-generated expert personas per task, distinct from the human experts who developed the taxonomy.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

RIFT taxonomy development uses 85 rubrics and 255 expert annotations across five sources with four refinement rounds; the intervention experiment separately uses 60 human-authored rubrics, 30 each from GDPval and Terminal-Bench.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Among 48 rubrics with nonconstant panel-rated necessity, 10 have negative weight-necessity rank correlation; Table 1 reports mean ordering correlation+0.195 for human-authored rubrics, scored by the model-persona panel.
